work.title: Counterexamples to the Mathieu Property: From Explicit Quotient Constructions to a General Classification
work.abstract:
In 1997, Olivier Mathieu conjectured that if every positive power of a function on a compact connected Lie group has average zero, then multiplying those powers by any fixed function should eventually preserve this property. Christopher D. Long disproved this conjecture in 2026 and classified the compact connected groups for which the property holds.

This paper extends that classification to a much broader family of algebraic spaces, including nonspherical homogeneous spaces and disconnected groups. We prove a necessary and sufficient condition determining exactly when the Mathieu–Zhao property holds.

The proof constructs new explicit counterexamples using the binary octahedral and icosahedral groups, covering cases not addressed by earlier classifications. These counterexamples remain valid under polynomial transformations and give rise to transcendental generating functions.

The main result completes the classification of the Mathieu–Zhao property for complex homogeneous spaces whose acting groups and stabilizers have reductive identity components, extending the known results from compact groups and spherical spaces to this general setting.

Human-understanding declaration: Some parts of this contribution, but not all, have been checked and understood by a human.
Additional provenance: This research was conducted through an iterative, AI-assisted mathematical research process.

I directed the research, selected the problems and approaches to investigate, evaluated the results, and took responsibility for the final mathematical claims.

ChatGPT (OpenAI) was used extensively as a research collaborator to explore mathematical constructions, develop and critique proof strategies, investigate existing literature, identify potential gaps, and assist with mathematical writing and verification code.

Python-based computational tools supported the investigation and checking of explicit algebraic identities and examples. The manuscript was prepared in LaTeX, with research materials maintained in a public GitHub repository.

The computational experiments and AI-generated arguments were treated as supporting material rather than mathematical proof. The submitted paper presents self-contained arguments intended to be independently verifiable.

The work is publicly available as a preprint and has not yet undergone independent peer review.
